newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN SET TO SIGN ZIEGE FROM BAYERN-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN SET TO SIGN ZIEGE FROM BAYERN-REPORT.

text.p: Italian champions AC Milan are set to sign Bayern Munich's Christian Ziege on a four-year contract paying three billion lire ($2 million) a year, sports daily Corriere dello Sport reported on Wednesday.
A club official had no immediate comment on the report.

The Italian newspaper quoted Bayern chairman Franz Beckenbauer as saying on a German television programme on Tuesday: "On the basis of information in our possession, Ziege will sign with Milan at the end of the current season."
The move was a blow for European champions Juventus who had been wooing the German player for months and had secured a commitment from him to join them next season, the newspaper said.
But Juventus were only prepared to pay wing-back Ziege an annual salary of two billion lire ($1.3 million), according to the Corriere.
Ziege's contract with Bayern contains a buyout clause allowing him to leave the club in June 1997 in exchange for a fee to the club of nine billion lire ($6 million).
